titulo: Module 06 — Exam: the agentic loop, enforcement with hooks, and human handoff

questoes.pergunta: A fintech runs a support agent in a manual loop on the Messages API. The loop ends when the response text contains "resolved" or "anything else I can help with". In some conversations, the customer receives "Your refund has been resolved, I'll process it now" and the refund never happens. What is the best fix?
opcoes: Instruct the model in the system prompt to use the word "resolved" only after calling all the tools
Add more closing phrases to the list to cover the variations
Decide whether to continue based on `stop_reason`: on `tool_use`, execute the tools and continue; stop only on `end_turn`
Force an extra iteration after detecting "resolved", just in case
questoes.explicacao: The model narrated ("I'll process it now") and requested the tool in the same turn. The reliable signal is `stop_reason`; reading the text is anti-pattern #1.
feedbacks: Tempting because it seems to "align" the model, but it still depends on natural language, which is probabilistic and ambiguous.
Attacks the symptom: it grows the word list, but the criterion is still text. Any new phrase breaks it again.
Correct. `stop_reason: tool_use` says there is a pending action; only `end_turn` ends the loop.
A hack: one more round doesn't guarantee that all the tools were executed, and it keeps the wrong criterion.

questoes.pergunta: In a CI pipeline, Claude generates a JSON review report. About 3% of runs fail to parse with "unexpected end of input", always on very large PRs. The code only checks whether the HTTP status was 200. What is the most likely cause, and the fix?
opcoes: The response was cut off (`stop_reason: max_tokens`); check `stop_reason` and handle the cutoff (raise the ceiling, continue, or split the PR)
The model is hallucinating invalid JSON; add few-shot with well-formed JSON
Network instability; add retry with backoff for all responses
The schema is too complex; remove fields from the report
questoes.explicacao: "Unexpected end" on large inputs is the signature of truncation by `max_tokens`. HTTP 200 doesn't guarantee a complete response: check `stop_reason`.
feedbacks: Correct. The cutoff happens in the middle of the JSON; `stop_reason` would have revealed it.
Tempting ("improve the prompt"), but the JSON isn't malformed, it's incomplete. Few-shot doesn't raise the output ceiling.
A blind retry repeats the same cutoff; it isn't a network failure, the response arrived with 200.
Reducing fields may mask the symptom, but it sacrifices requirements and doesn't address the cause (an undetected cutoff).

questoes.pergunta: A retailer's support agent requested `get_order`, `get_customer`, and `get_shipping` in the same response. The first two returned; `get_shipping` timed out. How should the harness build the next request?
opcoes: Send only the two successful results and let the model notice the absence of the third
Send three `user` messages, one per result, with the timeout last
Abort the conversation and ask the customer to try again later
Send a single `user` message with three `tool_result` blocks, each with its `tool_use_id`; the one for `get_shipping` with `is_error: true` and a description of the timeout
questoes.explicacao: Parallel tool use: every `tool_use` gets a `tool_result`, with exact ids, in a single `user` message; the failure goes with `is_error: true` so the model can decide how to recover.
feedbacks: Omitting the result breaks the protocol (every `tool_use` requires a response) and hides the failure.
Spreading them across several `user` messages violates the expected format for parallel results.
Aborting because of a transient failure wastes what has already been obtained; the model can retry or proceed without the shipping info.
Correct. A complete result, including the error, so the model can reason about it.

questoes.pergunta: A research team noticed that the agent sometimes consults academic sources before news, and wrote a router in C# that decides the next tool based on keywords in the question. Now the agent fails on questions that don't fit the rules. What is the best direction?
opcoes: Expand the router with more rules and a fallback for unrecognized questions
Give the decision of which tool to call, and when, back to the model, improving the tool descriptions if selection is poor
Train a classifier to choose the tool before each call
Fix the order news → academic → synthesis for every question
questoes.explicacao: In an agent, the model is the one that chooses the tool. An external decision tree is an anti-pattern; if selection fails, the simplest fix is the tool description.
feedbacks: Deepens the anti-pattern: more rules, more uncovered cases. It means maintaining a fragile script.
Correct. The model adapts its path to what it discovers; descriptions guide selection.
More complex than necessary: a classifier before looking at the descriptions violates "the simplest fix".
Turns the agent into a fixed pipeline; the order of sources isn't even a critical rule that would justify it.

questoes.pergunta: After an incident in which a research agent got stuck in a loop burning tokens for hours, an engineer proposes: "the loop always stops at the 8th iteration". Legitimate tasks typically take 3 to 25 iterations. What is the best decision?
opcoes: Accept 8 iterations, since that covers most tasks
Calculate the limit from the historical average number of iterations
Keep `end_turn` as the stopping criterion and add a backstop well above normal, with logging and an alert when it fires
Remove any limit and rely only on `stop_reason`
questoes.explicacao: A fixed limit as the primary mechanism is an anti-pattern; as a backstop against bugs, it's correct. The normal end is still `end_turn`.
feedbacks: It would cut off legitimate tasks of 9 to 25 iterations midway.
An average still cuts off everything above it; it's still an arbitrary number used as the criterion.
Correct. A high safety net + an alert, without changing the stopping criterion.
Overcorrection in the opposite direction: without a backstop, a bug repeats the incident.

questoes.pergunta: A productivity assistant uses the server-side web search tool. On questions that require many searches, users receive half-finished answers. The logs show `stop_reason: "pause_turn"` on those responses, which the code treats as final. What should be done?
opcoes: On receiving `pause_turn`, resend the conversation with the response appended as an assistant turn so the model can continue
Increase the request's `max_tokens`
Replace the server-side web search with a custom client-side tool
Build an empty `tool_result` for the pending search and resend
questoes.explicacao: `pause_turn` = the server-side loop hit its iteration cap. Resend so the model can resume.
feedbacks: Correct. It's a protocol pause, resolved by resending.
Confuses it with `max_tokens`. The cutoff here isn't on output; it's on the server-side loop.
Rewriting the integration is much more complex and unnecessary: the protocol already provides for continuation.
Server-side tools don't receive a `tool_result` from the client; that would break the conversation.

questoes.pergunta: A support agent, when it receives requests that violate the usage policy, sometimes returns a blank message to the customer. The code reads `content[0].text` whenever the HTTP status is 200. What is the appropriate fix?
opcoes: Treat every empty `content` as a network error and repeat the call
Add to the system prompt: "never give an empty response"
Use `tool_choice` to force a response tool on every call
Check `stop_reason` before reading `content` and handle `refusal` explicitly (appropriate message, logging, escalation where applicable)
questoes.explicacao: Refusals arrive with HTTP 200 and `stop_reason: refusal`. Code that ignores `stop_reason` treats them as an empty success.
feedbacks: It isn't a network error; repeating the call tends to produce the same refusal and masks the reason.
A prompt instruction changes neither the refusal behavior nor the fact that the code doesn't check the signal.
Forcing a tool isn't how refusals are handled and, on newer models, forcing a tool may not even be accepted.
Correct. The signal exists and needs to be handled.

questoes.pergunta: An audit showed that in about 2% of conversations, the support agent called `process_refund` before `verify_identity`. The system prompt already says, in capital letters, that verification is mandatory. What is the best fix?
opcoes: Repeat the rule at the end of the system prompt and in every user message
Programmatically block `process_refund` (a `PreToolUse` hook or a prerequisite in the tool) until the identity has been verified
Add few-shot examples showing the correct order
Use a second model to review each conversation before the refund
questoes.explicacao: A rule with financial consequences requires deterministic enforcement. A prompt (however emphatic), few-shot, and an LLM reviewer are all still probabilistic.
feedbacks: It may reduce the rate, but it won't eliminate it: this is the "critical rule only in the prompt" anti-pattern.
Correct. Deterministic: without verification, the refund doesn't execute.
Few-shot improves the average; it's still probabilistic.
More expensive, slower, and still probabilistic.

questoes.pergunta: An architect wants to guarantee that no refund is executed without identity verification in a support agent built with the Agent SDK. Which measures provide this guarantee? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: A `PreToolUse` hook that denies `process_refund` (`permissionDecision: "deny"`) when the session has no recorded verification
A "Critical rules" section at the top of the system prompt
A `prompt`-type hook that asks an LLM whether the conversation looks verified
Make `process_refund` require a `verification_token` issued by `verify_identity`, rejecting the call without a valid token
A `PostToolUse` hook on `process_refund` that raises an alert when there was no verification
questoes.explicacao: Guarantee = deterministic code before execution: a `PreToolUse` hook that denies, or a prerequisite validated by the tool itself.
feedbacks: Correct. Deterministic blocking before the tool runs.
A prompt is probabilistic; it doesn't guarantee anything.
Tempting because it's a hook, but the `prompt` type is an LLM decision: still probabilistic, for something that has an objective criterion.
Correct. The prerequisite in the tool's code is deterministic.
`PostToolUse` runs afterward: the refund has already been made. An alert isn't prevention.

questoes.pergunta: Human support staff complain that when the support agent transfers a case, they have to read the entire conversation and often redo the identity verification. Which change solves this best?
opcoes: Attach the full transcript to the ticket, highlighting the customer's messages
Ask the agent for a one-sentence summary before transferring
Create a handoff tool with a structured schema: customer and verification status, issue, order, root cause, actions taken, reason for escalation, recommended action, and amount
Transfer earlier, so conversations are shorter
questoes.explicacao: The human typically doesn't read the transcript. The handoff needs a structured summary, with fixed fields that guarantee completeness (including what has already been done).
feedbacks: Still requires reading the transcript; it doesn't say what has already been done or what is recommended.
A single sentence of free prose forgets fields (e.g., verification already done) and is inconsistent.
Correct. Required fields = a complete, actionable handoff.
Attacks the wrong symptom and worsens automatic resolution; the problem is the quality of the handoff.

questoes.pergunta: A team uses Claude Code in a monorepo and wants any attempt by Claude to edit `.env` files to be blocked, for all developers. Which configuration achieves this?
opcoes: A `PreToolUse` hook with matcher `Edit|Write` in the project's `.claude/settings.json`, with a script that blocks (exit 2) when the path is `.env`
An instruction in the project's CLAUDE.md: "never edit .env files"
A `PostToolUse` hook in `.claude/settings.local.json` that undoes the edit
A `PreToolUse` hook in the tech lead's `~/.claude/settings.json`
questoes.explicacao: Block beforehand = `PreToolUse`; apply to the team = versioned project settings. Exit 2 blocks and explains the reason to Claude.
feedbacks: Correct. The right event, a shared location, deterministic blocking.
CLAUDE.md is an instruction: probabilistic, it doesn't block.
Incorrect on two counts: `PostToolUse` acts after the edit, and `settings.local.json` is personal (gitignored).
User settings apply only to the tech lead, not to the team.

questoes.pergunta: A healthcare company uses a productivity agent connected to a medical records MCP server. Requirement: the model must never see patients' CPF numbers or full names, and no user can disable this protection. Which measures meet this requirement? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Instruct the model in CLAUDE.md to ignore any CPFs it finds
A `PostToolUse` hook on the medical records server's tools that masks CPF and name before the result reaches the model
A `PreToolUse` hook that blocks all calls to the medical records server
Configure the hook in `.claude/settings.local.json` on each machine
Distribute the hook configuration via the organization's managed policy
questoes.explicacao: Processing the result = `PostToolUse` (mask PII). "No one can disable it" = managed policy, which sits above user/project settings.
feedbacks: The data would already be in context; an instruction doesn't stop the model from seeing it.
Correct. Normalizes/masks the result before it reaches the model.
Solves privacy by killing the functionality; the goal is to use the medical records without exposing PII.
Local is personal, and any user can change it or simply not have it.
Correct. Organization policy, which the user can't override.

questoes.pergunta: In a repository, a developer proposes a `PostToolUse` hook on `Bash` that detects `rm -rf` in the executed command and returns an error to Claude, to "prevent accidental deletions". What is the correct assessment?
opcoes: Appropriate, since Claude will read the error and won't repeat the command
Inappropriate: `PostToolUse` runs after execution; to prevent it, use `PreToolUse` with blocking (exit 2 or `permissionDecision: "deny"`)
Appropriate, as long as the hook is of type `agent`
Inappropriate: hooks can't inspect `Bash` commands
questoes.explicacao: Block = Pre; process the result = Post. By the time `PostToolUse` runs, the files have already been deleted.
feedbacks: The damage has already been done; avoiding a repeat isn't prevention.
Correct. Prevention happens before execution.
The hook type doesn't change when the event fires.
False: the event includes `tool_input`, including the `Bash` command.

questoes.pergunta: An engineer wrote a `command` hook on `PreToolUse` to block `git push --force`. The script prints the reason and ends with `exit 1`, but the push still goes through. What is the problem?
opcoes: The matcher needs to be `*` for Bash hooks
`command` hooks can't block; only `http` hooks can
To block, the script must end with exit 2 (reason on stderr) or return `permissionDecision: "deny"` with exit 0
Blocking only works in `PostToolUse`
questoes.explicacao: Exit 0 passes, exit 2 blocks (stderr goes back to Claude). Other codes are non-blocking errors: the action proceeds.
feedbacks: The matcher can be specific (e.g., `Bash`); the problem is the exit code.
False: the `command` hook is exactly the deterministic type that blocks with exit 2.
Correct. Exit 1 is a non-blocking error.
Backwards: blocking is the job of `PreToolUse`.

questoes.pergunta: A company is going to build a support agent that needs specialized subagents, compliance hooks, resumable sessions, and access to policy files on disk. Which way of building it makes the most sense?
opcoes: Claude Agent SDK, which provides the Claude Code harness (built-in tools, subagents, hooks, sessions) as a library
A manual loop on the Messages API, implementing subagents, hooks, and sessions from scratch
The SDK's Tool Runner, which runs the tool loop
A single API call with all the policies in the prompt
questoes.explicacao: When the requirements include subagents, hooks, sessions, and file tools, the Agent SDK is the simplest option that meets them (anything else would mean reimplementing the harness).
feedbacks: Correct. The requirements match what the SDK already provides.
Possible, but it means reinventing the harness: more code, more risk.
Tool Runner handles the tool loop, but it doesn't provide subagents, hooks, or sessions.
It isn't an agent: there's no loop, no tools, and no enforcement.

questoes.pergunta: A team needs an extractor that receives an order email, calls a catalog lookup tool and a shipping calculation tool, and returns JSON. There are no files, subagents, or sessions. The initial proposal is to use Managed Agents with a coordinator and two subagents. What is the best recommendation?
opcoes: Keep the proposal, since subagents make the system more scalable
Use the Agent SDK with one subagent per tool
Use Managed Agents without subagents, to avoid operating infrastructure
A manual loop or Tool Runner with the two tools, which is the simplest option that works
questoes.explicacao: Choose the simplest option that solves the problem. Two tools and JSON output justify neither multi-agent orchestration nor hosted infrastructure.
feedbacks: Hypothetical scalability doesn't justify present complexity; it violates "start simple".
One subagent per tool is unnecessary decomposition, and more expensive.
Simpler than the proposal, but the question doesn't call for a sandbox or hosted execution; it's still more than necessary.
Correct. A direct loop with two tools.

questoes.pergunta: A research system sometimes consumes far more tokens than expected. To limit cost, someone reduced `max_tokens` from 8,000 to 1,500. Now the reports arrive cut off in the middle, and the total cost has barely dropped. What would be the appropriate approach?
opcoes: Reduce `max_tokens` even further and ask for short responses in the prompt
Give the agent a visible task budget, so it can prioritize and deliver something complete within the limit, while keeping a backstop
Remove search tools to reduce the number of calls
End the loop when the accumulated text exceeds N characters
questoes.explicacao: `max_tokens` is invisible and per response: it cuts off output without reducing the number of rounds. A visible budget lets the model organize itself to fit.
feedbacks: Deepens the problem: more cutoffs, same number of rounds.
Correct. Visible → the model plans; the backstop protects against overruns.
Cripples the system's capability instead of controlling spend.
An arbitrary text-based stopping criterion, still producing cut-off reports.

questoes.pergunta: Regarding `stop_reason` handling in an agentic loop, which statements are correct? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: `pause_turn` indicates that a server-side tool loop has paused; resending the response lets it continue
`refusal` arrives with HTTP 200, so the code needs to check `stop_reason` before reading the content
`max_tokens` indicates that the model finished after using the entire available budget
`model_context_window_exceeded` means the request was rejected and nothing was generated
`end_turn` is reliable only if the final text contains an explicit confirmation
questoes.explicacao: `pause_turn` → resend; `refusal` → HTTP 200. `max_tokens` is a cutoff (not completion); an exceeded window produces valid but truncated output; `end_turn` makes reading the text unnecessary.
feedbacks: Correct.
Correct.
Tempting because of the name, but it means a cutoff midway: the response is incomplete.
There is generated output, valid but truncated, not a rejection.
`end_turn` is already the structured end signal; requiring a textual confirmation reintroduces the anti-pattern.

questoes.pergunta: An airline's policy says that refunds above $500 require a supervisor's approval. Today this is in the system prompt, and the agent sometimes approves $620 on its own. Which design is best?
opcoes: Ask the model to state its confidence and escalate when it is below 80%
Escalate every refund, regardless of the amount
Enforce the limit in code (the refund tool or a hook rejects anything above $500 with a structured error), and the agent escalates via a structured handoff
Repeat the limit with example amounts in the prompt
questoes.explicacao: A financial limit is a critical rule: deterministic code. Above the limit, the agent escalates to the supervisor with a structured summary.
feedbacks: Self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated; the criterion here is objective (the amount).
Overkill: it overloads humans with cases the agent can resolve.
Correct. Deterministic at the limit, a useful handoff above it.
Still probabilistic, just as it is today.

questoes.pergunta: In a code generation workflow with Claude Code, the team notices that Claude sometimes finishes by saying "implementation complete" while tests are still failing. They want to prevent it from ending the turn while the suite isn't passing, without relying on the model's discipline. What is the appropriate mechanism?
opcoes: Add to CLAUDE.md: "only say complete when all tests pass"
A `PostToolUse` hook on `Edit` that runs the tests after each edit
A `SessionEnd` hook that runs the tests and logs the result
A `Stop` hook that runs the suite and, if it fails, blocks the stop by returning the reason to Claude
questoes.explicacao: The `Stop` event fires when the agent is about to end its turn; blocking there forces Claude to continue, with the reason (failing tests) in hand.
feedbacks: An instruction is probabilistic; it's exactly the model's discipline that you want to stop relying on.
Gives useful feedback, but doesn't prevent ending the turn with failing tests.
`SessionEnd` fires at the end of the session: too late to make Claude continue.
Correct. A deterministic gate at the moment of stopping.
